reference_context.title: GNU C / ld Documentation
reference_context.document: Using the GNU Compiler Collection (GCC): Options for Code Generation Conventions
reference_context.snippet: The default is -fno-common, which specifies that the compiler places uninitialized global variables in the BSS section of the object file. This inhibits the merging of tentative definitions by the linker so you get a multiple-definition error if the same variable is accidentally defined in more than one compilation unit.

expected.root_cause: counter is defined (with an initializer) in globals.h, which is included by two .cpp files, so it is defined twice at link time.
expected.fix: Use `extern int counter;` in globals.h and `int counter = 0;` in one .cpp file.
